title: Custom ML-conventions skill
body:
> Use the bundled machine-learning guidance for product APIs. Create a skill named hol-ml-review that adds only our team's gates:
> 1. Fixed seed, recorded dataset dates and version.
> 2. Features come before the snapshot cutoff; labels cover the following 90 days and must be fully observed.
> 3. Temporal holdout with overlapping label windows purged. Fit preprocessing on training data only. No future outcomes or identifiers as predictors.
> 4. Compare a small baseline with the candidate on MAE and RMSE. Don't tune on the final holdout.
> 5. Register the exact feature signature, metrics and data metadata; verify warehouse inference.
> 6. Drift needs baseline data and performance needs ground truth; report pending or insufficient data honestly.
> 7. Writes stay in HOL_SANDBOX.P001. Stop before new compute, grants, deployment or external sharing.
>
> Then review the design before training.

Expected/check: custom skill adds team-specific gates without copying the whole bundled ML workflow. Recovery: edit one rule in the prepared skill. Explain SKILL.md frontmatter, workflow, and optional resource files.

title: Inspect data and point-in-time features
body:
> Inspect the prepared dataset's schema and counts. Show three customer snapshots with feature cutoff and label-end timestamps. Confirm no predictor uses transactions from its label window, and that the evaluation window is fully observed. Create the approved small feature dataset only in my sandbox schema.

Expected/check: data window checks, explicit feature list, zero-spend outcomes retained, no leakage. Recovery: precomputed feature checkpoint with the same documented boundaries.

title: Train and evaluate regression
body:
> Train a small regression baseline and one candidate using the approved temporal split. Use fixed random seeds and bounded model size. Evaluate MAE and RMSE, show the comparison against the baseline, and explain errors. Do not tune on the final holdout or provision a compute pool.

Expected/check: actual metrics, training/evaluation row counts and dates, no train/holdout overlap. Recovery: use the rehearsed model artifact, clearly label it prepared and retain its version and evaluation record. In Snowsight, verify the notebook kernel before running cells; use dedicated notebook tools when available.

technologies.name: Regression metrics
technologies.description: MAE and RMSE compared against a simple baseline

situation: You have clean features. Now find out whether a real model beats a simple baseline, honestly, on later data it hasn't seen.

tips.text: Always compare against the baseline. A model that barely beats "predict last quarter's spend" may not be worth deploying.
Don't tune on the final holdout. Once you do, it stops being a fair test.

concepts.definition: Train on earlier snapshots, evaluate on later ones, so the test mirrors real use.
MAE is the typical error in dollars; RMSE punishes large misses more.

title: Registry and warehouse batch inference
body:
> Register the selected model in HOL_SANDBOX.P001 with evaluation metrics, data seed/date range, feature signature, and intended WAREHOUSE target. Run batch predictions through the registered version on a small scoring cohort. Save IDs, snapshot timestamps, model/version, features, and predictions in a sandbox table.

Expected/check: model is visible in the Registry, metric metadata matches evaluated results, warehouse inference succeeds, output cardinality and finite predictions are checked. Recovery: run the prepared registered version; never report a locally computed prediction as warehouse inference.

title: Monitoring setup and UI
body:
> Configure a model-version monitor for the registered regression version using our historical scoring table and baseline. Include prediction and actual numeric score columns and TIMESTAMP_NTZ event times. Inspect the current drift and MAE/RMSE metrics, compare to the approved numeric thresholds, and summarize breached/not breached/insufficient data. Show the monitor in Snowsight.

Prepare during T-3: baseline and shifted historical cohorts spanning multiple days, fully observed labels, an actual model monitor and populated UI. Example teaching thresholds are PSI > 0.20 and MAE > 1.20 times baseline MAE; label them illustrative, define columns/time windows, and compute real values. If baseline MAE is zero, do not divide by zero: use an approved absolute threshold or mark comparison undefined.

Current model-version monitors require daily aggregation and valid numeric predictions/actuals; ground truth is required for performance metrics and baseline for drift. Do not assume a generic `accuracy` metric or an arbitrary `set_threshold()` method exists. Threshold comparison can be explicit queries; alert configuration is separate. A newly created monitor may not have refreshed: show `pending` and demonstrate the rehearsed reference monitor, not fabricated successful metrics. Display the last refresh/time window in the UI walkthrough.

technologies.description: Tracks drift and accuracy for a registered model version over time

technologies.description: View drift and performance charts for the monitored version

situation: Customer behavior shifts after a promotion. You need to know when the model's predictions drift or its error grows, before the business notices.

tips.text: Monitors need history: a baseline for drift and actual outcomes for accuracy. A brand-new monitor may show pending until it refreshes.
The thresholds here (PSI > 0.20, MAE > 1.2x baseline) are teaching examples. Agree real ones with the business.

concepts.definition: A change in the distribution of inputs or predictions compared to a baseline (e.g. PSI).
Comparing predictions to actual outcomes once they arrive (MAE, RMSE).

title: Recap and optional SPCS path
body: Review skill, temporal correctness, registry, inference, and monitoring. Optional follow-on: approved SPCS compute pool, supported model target, authenticated REST endpoint, small bounded request set, p50/p95/p99 measured latency including warm/cold distinctions, and explicit teardown. Never enable a public endpoint or provision SPCS merely for a slide.

tips.text: Real-time serving (SPCS) is worth it only when batch scoring can't meet the need. Measure latency before promising it.
